description: Phase 9a gate — CREATE INDEX statement + empty-index storage scaffold. Grammar: `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX <name> ON <table> (<col>, ...)`. Two new reserved keywords: INDEX, UNIQUE. One new VDBE opcode: `CreateIndex { name, table, columns, unique }`. One new file-format surface: empty index-leaf page (type 0x0a, cell_count=0). sqlite_schema now accepts type='index' rows. NO backfill of existing table rows (→9b), NO DML maintenance (→9c), NO query planner usage (→9d), NO UNIQUE enforcement (→9g), NO DROP INDEX (→9f). New errors: STORAGE_INDEX_EXISTS, COMPILE_DUPLICATE_INDEX_COLUMN. max_invariant=28 unchanged. All phase1..6t fixtures must stay green.

cases.name: create-unique-index-syntactically-accepted
cases.description: UNIQUE is accepted syntactically in 9a. Enforcement is deferred to 9g — two INSERTs of the same value do NOT error in 9a (index is empty and stale; UNIQUE unenforced).

program.sql: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_x ON t (x);
CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b TEXT, c INTEGER);
CREATE INDEX idx_abc ON t (a, b, c);
Create Unique Index idx_b On t (x);

cases.name: create-index-name-case-preserved
cases.description: Index name is case-preserved as parsed; a subsequent CREATE INDEX with the SAME NAME regardless of case still collides (case-insensitive name-collision test in a separate fixture).

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
CREATE INDEX idx ON t (x, x);
CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER, z INTEGER);
CREATE INDEX idx ON t (x, y, x);
CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);

cases.name: create-index-name-collides-with-table
cases.description: Index names share the same namespace as table names in sqlite_schema.

cases.name: create-table-name-collides-with-index
cases.description: Symmetric: creating a table with the same name as an existing index fails with the existing STORAGE_TABLE_EXISTS error (names share the same sqlite_schema namespace).

program.sql: CREATE INDEX idx ON t x;
CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
CREATE INDEX idx ON t (x, y,);

cases.name: index-keyword-as-index-name-rejected
cases.description: `CREATE INDEX index ON t(x)` is a parse error because the second token must be an IDENTIFIER, not the reserved keyword INDEX itself.

cases.name: create-index-then-inserts-still-work
cases.description: Phase 9a does NOT maintain indexes on INSERT (deferred to 9c). Table INSERTs after CREATE INDEX still succeed and are visible via plain SELECT (which doesn't use the index, so staleness is invisible).

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x;

cases.name: create-index-with-prior-data-stays-empty
cases.description: Phase 9a does NOT backfill from existing rows (deferred to 9b). Tests cannot observe the index's emptiness directly via SELECT (no query-planner integration yet), but the INSERT+SELECT path remains correct because it never touches the index.

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x;
CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER, c TEXT);
CREATE INDEX idx_ab ON t (a, b);

cases.name: index-on-different-tables-independent-namespace-for-columns
cases.description: Column names are validated against the specific target table. An index on t1(x) does not care whether t2 has a column `x`.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t1 (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE t2 (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);

cases.name: index-name-collision-case-sensitivity
cases.description: sqlite_schema name-collision is case-insensitive per standard SQL convention (like SQLite's) — `idx` and `IDX` collide.
